result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex against lib/letflow/design/req049-variable-merge.md and .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions. SPECIFIC ADJUDICATION (batch-rejection semantics): design doc §3.1 step 5 and §3.2 explicitly specify all-or-nothing whole-batch rejection -- 'one rejected key aborts the entire incoming_variables batch, not just that key... not even the new_keys inserts that would otherwise have succeeded are applied' -- with the reasoning stated inline (an instance-level ERROR halt is incompatible with some of the same batch's variables having already merged, and a worse audit story than nothing-landed). The implementation's find_rejection/2 scans overwrite_keys only, and on finding a rejection returns {:rejected, current_variables, [event]} -- current_variables is the original argument, unmodified, so neither the rejected key's overwrite nor any of the same call's new_keys inserts are applied. This exactly matches the design's §3.1/§3.2 algorithm; ELIXIR-DEV's self-review note ('mixed-batch abort on first rejected key, new_keys not inserted either') describes intended behavior, not a divergence. No FAIL here. Q1 idiomatic vs crutch: N/A gen_statem concern -- this is a pure Map/Enum-only kernel module (Letflow.Engine.Transition precedent), no state machine or process involved; style is idiomatic (Enum.split_with, Enum.reduce, Enum.find_value, no manual recursion where stdlib suffices). Q2 supervision: N/A, pure function module, holds no state, spawns nothing, matches design §1's 'no Ecto schema, no migration, no DB table' scope. Q3 type-safety: no new gap beyond what req044-transition-kernel.md's precedent already established (plain tagged-tuple events, not structs) -- consistent with the existing convention, not a new instance requiring a docs/issues/ filing. Q4 scope creep: none -- module is scoped exactly to merge/3 and its types, no behaviours/macros/premature abstraction; purity grep check (Repo./Logger./Registry.validate_payload/etc.) returns matches only inside @moduledoc/@typedoc prose (the module's own documentation quoting REQ-024's function names and the verification grep command itself), zero matches in actual executable code -- confirms the purity claim. Checked against docs/anti-patterns.md: no entry applies to this diff; the design doc's own §0 already followed the 'targeted awk read of requirements.yaml' anti-pattern fix correctly.
